That’s far from the only promise he’s broken.

Trump repeatedly promised on the campaign trail to cap credit card interest rates at 10 percent.

But since he took office, Americans have paid nearly $240.7B in credit card interest — $134.5B more than what they would have paid under a 10 percent cap.

Like so many of his promises, it was another lie. piped.video/watch?v=vZwV58Dd…

What was partying with JFK Jr. in the 1990s like?

I remember like it was yesterday.

Getting big money out of our politics and raising taxes on the super-wealthy are both possible — not easy, but possible. They’re also necessary to reverse the mounting corruption that’s undermining our system. Some thoughts... https://robertreich.substack.com/p/why-are-the-wealthy-pouring-so-much

Remember: The richest 1% evade roughly $160 billion in taxes every year.

That amount would fund SNAP for a year with money to spare.

Ask yourself who the real freeloaders are.

In three months, Zohran Mamdani has:

-Delivered millions in restitution for workers cheated by fast food and delivery companies
-Cracked down on bad landlords
-Launched the first stage of a universal childcare program
-Fixed thousands of potholes in NYC streets

This is what leadership looks like.

A tool that helps thousands of communities decide when to evacuate residents during hurricanes will expire tomorrow.

Why? Because of Kristi Noem’s DHS policy to personally approve expenses over $100K, which is still in place.

But she had time to spend $220 million on ads. Priorities.

Mere months into 2026, just 50 American billionaires have already pumped a jaw-dropping $433 MILLION into the midterm elections — the overwhelming majority of which has benefitted Republicans.

Citizens United is corrupting our system every day.

Many of you may be celebrating MLB’s Opening Day today — but I suspect your wallets aren’t.

The average cost for a family of four to attend an MLB game is a whopping $226, from tickets to parking to concessions.

But there’s a way we can fight price-gouging at the ballpark. Watch.

Gas. Heating costs. Electricity. Groceries. 

Every single thing that working families can't opt out of is getting more expensive at once.

At least 163 people have so far been killed in US boat bombings.

Remember: No judge or jury has found these boats were trafficking drugs. We're taking Trump's word for it.

This is a danger to us all.

Should it work mainly for big corporations and billionaires? Or should it work for the rest of us?
